1→# COMFYUI-3D-VIEWPORT — STRATEGY
     2→## Dual-Track: Agent Graft Layer (Now) → Standalone Viewport (Future)
     3→## Date: 2026-02-19
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## What This Project Actually Is
     8→
     9→**comfyui-3D-viewport** started as a graft layer for `comfyui-agent` — adding 3D ecosystem intelligence to the agent's four capability layers. Grafts A–D shipped (665 tests green). The project is now evolving toward a second track: a standalone 3D viewport with real cinematographic cameras that outputs LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data.
    10→
    11→**Two tracks, one convergence point:**
    12→
    13→| Track | Status | Tech Stack | Ships Value As |
    14→|-------|--------|------------|----------------|
    15→| Agent Graft | Grafts A–D shipped, E pending | Python (parent codebase) | Agent understands 3D workflows |
    16→| Standalone Viewport | Planning phase | TBD (C++/Hydra or Python/Three.js) | Real-camera 3D viewport for ComfyUI |
    17→
    18→Both tracks output LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data. The agent understands it (graft track). The viewport generates it (viewport track).
    19→
    20→---
    21→
    22→## Track 1: Agent Graft Layer (Current)
    23→
    24→### What Shipped
    25→
    26→| Graft | Layer | What It Added |
    27→|-------|-------|---------------|
    28→| A | UNDERSTAND | MESH, VOXEL, POINT_CLOUD, CAMERA, POSE type recognition |
    29→| B | DISCOVER | Partner Node `source_tier` + comparative knowledge |
    30→| C | DISCOVER | Splat-to-mesh conversion paths with pitfall warnings |
    31→| D | DISCOVER | Viewport tool discovery (VNCCS, Action Director, 3DView) |
    32→
    33→### What's Next
    34→
    35→| Phase | What | Depends On | Type |
    36→|-------|------|------------|------|
    37→| **Verify** | Confirm grafts work conversationally | Nothing | Audit |
    38→| **Fix Routing** | Wire knowledge to trigger keywords if gaps found | Verify | Code (minor) |
    39→| **Graft E Prep** | Mock workflows + test fixtures for demo scenarios | Nothing | Test infra |
    40→| **Camera Pipeline** | Teach agent about Load3D → AdvancedCameraControlNode | LOAD3D_CAMERA schema | Knowledge |
    41→| **Graft E** | Demo scenarios (splat-to-mesh, ControlNet 3D, partner comparison) | Phase 5 Multi-Pipe | Integration |
    42→
    43→### Integration With Existing ComfyUI Ecosystem
    44→
    45→ComfyUI already has a camera pipeline:
    46→
    47→```
    48→Load3D → LOAD3D_CAMERA → AdvancedCameraControlNode → prompt generation
    49→```
    50→
    51→The agent graft layer teaches the agent about this pipeline. When a user asks "how do I control camera angle?", the agent surfaces this workflow with specific node names and recommendations.
    52→
    53→The future viewport will plug into this same pipeline — outputting LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data with extended cinematographic metadata.
    54→
    55→---
    56→
    57→## Track 2: Standalone Viewport (Future)
    58→
    59→### The Vision
    60→A professional 3D viewport that renders with real camera bodies and lenses, outputs depth/normal AOVs through real sensor projection, and sends them to ComfyUI for AI generation.
    61→
    62→The unfair advantage: 16 years of cinematography expertise. Not a game engine camera. An ARRI Alexa 35 with a Cooke Anamorphic/i 40mm. The depth map looks different because the projection math is different.
    63→
    64→### Architecture Decision (Pending)
    65→
    66→Three paths — owner chooses:
    67→
    68→**Custom Node** (Python + Three.js)
    69→- Installs via ComfyUI-Manager
    70→- Browser-based viewport like Load3D
    71→- Huge distribution, easy install
    72→- Limited to Three.js rendering (no Hydra AOVs, no true sensor projection)
    73→
    74→**Standalone App** (C++ / Qt / Hydra)
    75→- Real Hydra/Storm rendering
    76→- True sensor projection matrices
    77→- Cooke anamorphic squeeze in actual math
    78→- Professional tool, harder to distribute
    79→- CarWash codebase as proven reference for ComfyUI client code
    80→
    81→**Hybrid**
    82→- Custom node for distribution, standalone app for production
    83→- Both output LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data
    84→- Agent works with either seamlessly
    85→- Two codebases
    86→
    87→### Data Contract
    88→
    89→Both tracks speak the same language — LOAD3D_CAMERA JSON:
    90→
    91→```
    92→Standard fields (Load3D compatibility):
    93→  position, target, up, fov, focal_length
    94→
    95→Extended fields (cinematographic — carwash_ prefix):
    96→  carwash_sensor_body, carwash_sensor_gate
    97→  carwash_sensor_width_mm, carwash_sensor_height_mm
    98→  carwash_lens_model, carwash_squeeze_ratio
    99→  carwash_t_stop, carwash_lens_metadata_protocol
   100→  carwash_aov_passes
   101→```
   102→
   103→Standard fields work with existing ComfyUI nodes. Extended fields unlock cinematographic features for the viewport.
   104→
   105→### Reference Codebases
   106→
   107→| Codebase | What We Take | License |
   108→|----------|-------------|---------|
   109→| CarWash | ComfyUI client patterns (WebSocket, HTTP, PNG encoding), framebuffer, FNV-1a determinism | Owner's own code |
   110→| Gaffer | Hydra viewport embedding in Qt, scene graph patterns | BSD |
   111→| ComfyUI Load3D | LOAD3D_CAMERA schema, camera data contract | GPL |
   112→
   113→### Camera + Lens Database
   114→
   115→Shared reference data for both tracks:
   116→
   117→- **Camera bodies:** ARRI Alexa 35, RED V-RAPTOR, Sony VENICE 2 (expandable)
   118→- **Lenses:** Cooke Anamorphic/i, Cooke S7/i, Atlas Orion (expandable)
   119→- **Format:** JSON with sensor dimensions, max resolution, native ISO, t-stop ranges
   120→- **Location:** `data/camera_lens_database.json` in this repo
   121→
   122→This database serves both the viewport (projection math) and the agent (knowledge for recommendations).
   123→
   124→---
   125→
   126→## Convergence Plan
   127→
   128→```
   129→NOW                          NEAR TERM                    FUTURE
   130→───────────────────────      ───────────────────────      ─────────────────────
   131→Agent knows 3D types         Agent knows camera pipeline  Agent drives viewport
   132→  (Grafts A-D ✓)              (Phase 4)                    (tool API)
   133→
   134→                             Viewport architecture doc    Viewport ships
   135→                               (Phase 5)                   (new exec spec)
   136→
   137→                             Camera/lens database          Both output
   138→                               (Phase 5)                   LOAD3D_CAMERA
   139→```
   140→
   141→Convergence happens when:
   142→1. Agent understands LOAD3D_CAMERA data (Phase 4)
   143→2. Viewport outputs LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data (future)
   144→3. Agent gains tool API to drive viewport (future)
   145→
   146→Each step ships value independently. No step blocks another.
   147→
   148→---
   149→
   150→## Risk Register
   151→
   152→| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
   153→|------|-----------|--------|------------|
   154→| LOAD3D_CAMERA schema changes in ComfyUI update | Medium | High | Pin to discovered schema, version the carwash_ extensions |
   155→| USD/Hydra build complexity blocks standalone viewport | High | Medium | Start with custom node path, upgrade to Hydra later |
   156→| Partner Node list goes stale | Medium | Low | Quarterly review cycle, hardcoded is fine for now |
   157→| Graft knowledge stored but never surfaced | Medium | High | Phase 1 verification catches this early |
   158→| Agent Phase 5 (Multi-Pipe) delayed, blocking Graft E | Medium | Low | Graft E prep (mock workflows, tests) can proceed independently |
   159→
   160→---
   161→
   162→## Execution Spec
   163→
   164→See `EXECUTION_SPEC.md` for detailed phase-by-phase instructions for Claude Code.
   165→
   166→**Quick start:**
   167→```
   168→Read EXECUTION_SPEC.md. Execute Phase 1. Report at gate.
   169→```
   170→
